scientific_explanation.question_what: Regional spatial distribution of Precipitation Corrected (PRECTOTCORR, mm/day) across 66 native NASA assimilation grid cells from 1981 to 2023. Critically, the domain exhibits contrasting spatial trend directions: 55 cells display increasing trends while 11 cells display decreasing trends.
scientific_explanation.question_where: Rectangular geographic bounding domain (Lat 8.5° to 13.5° N, Lon 76.5° to 80.5° E); it is not an administrative boundary.
scientific_explanation.question_how_much: The domain exhibits a pronounced spatial dipole: 55 cells exhibit increasing trends (peaking at +0.329 mm/day/decade), whereas 11 cells exhibit decreasing trends (dropping to -0.438 mm/day/decade). The net domain-wide mean Sen's trend rate is +0.090 mm/day/decade.
scientific_explanation.question_are_changes_significant: 34 of 66 grid cells (51.5%) demonstrate statistically significant trends at the local α = 0.05 level (18 remain significant after Benjamini-Hochberg False Discovery Rate control). Importantly, local significance counts by direction are: 27 increasing cells (14 under FDR control) and 7 decreasing cells (4 under FDR control) meet rigorous significance thresholds.
scientific_explanation.scientific_synthesis: Estimated trends vary across the selected bounding box. 14 positive and 4 negative estimates pass the per-variable Benjamini-Hochberg procedure. These exploratory results do not establish causes, and spatial dependence affects interpretation.
scientific_limitations: Spatial Boundary Truncation: Grid cells located along coastlines incorporate mixed land-ocean surface boundary layer physics.
Multiple Testing Considerations: When testing dozens of spatial cells simultaneously, False Discovery Rate (FDR) control is necessary to verify true regional significance.
Model Resolution: 0.5° latitude x 0.625° longitude (~50 km) resolution cannot resolve fine-scale micro-topographic valleys in mountainous corridors.
scientific_explanation.citation: NASA POWER Project, NASA Langley Research Center (NASA GMAO MERRA-2 (Precipitation gauge-calibrated)). Data retrieved under MERRA-2 assimilation framework.

scientific_explanation.question_what: The observed Earth-system parameter is Temperature at 2 Meters (T2M), measured in °C. Across the 43-year record (1981–2023), the data demonstrates warming. The baseline climatological mean over this period is -6.77 °C (standard deviation: ±1.40 °C).
scientific_explanation.question_where: Observed at Svalbard (Arctic) (78.2200° N, 15.6300° E), representative of the source grid cell (0.5° latitude x 0.625° longitude (~50 km)) over Svalbard, Norway (Arctic Zone).
scientific_explanation.question_how_much: The non-parametric Sen's median slope indicates a change rate of +0.805 °C per decade (+0.0805 °C/year) with a 95% confidence interval of [+0.587 to +1.042] °C/decade. Over the full 43-year observational window, the cumulative estimated shift is +3.38 °C (+50.0% relative to baseline). For comparison, standard parametric linear regression (OLS) yields +0.787 °C/decade (R² = 0.50).
scientific_explanation.question_are_changes_significant: YES, the observed trend is statistically significant (p < 0.001 (Extremely Significant)). The rank-based Mann-Kendall test yields standardized test statistic Z = +5.02 and p = 0.00000, rejecting the null hypothesis of no trend at the 95% confidence level (α = 0.05). Accounting for positive serial lag-1 autocorrelation (r₁ = 0.56), the autocorrelation-adjusted Mann-Kendall test confirms p = 0.0000.
scientific_explanation.scientific_synthesis: Based on NASA NASA Global Modeling and Assimilation Office (GMAO) MERRA-2 data (1981–2023), Svalbard (Arctic) exhibits a robust, statistically significant upward trajectory in temperature at 2 meters. The consistency between the non-parametric Sen's slope (+0.805 °C/dec) and OLS slope (+0.787 °C/dec) does not establish the cause of the estimated trend.
scientific_limitations: Spatial Gridding: NASA MERRA-2 assimilation native grid is 0.5° latitude x 0.625° longitude (~50 km). Sub-grid urban microclimate variations (e.g. localized urban canyon heat islands) are spatially smoothed.

Reanalysis Assimilation: Surface meteorological fields are derived from the NASA GEOS atmospheric general circulation model assimilating satellite sounders and conventional weather stations rather than an isolated single in-situ thermometer.

Serial Autocorrelation: Earth system climate time series frequently possess interannual persistence (e.g., ENSO, Indian Ocean Dipole). Modified Mann-Kendall variance adjustments were applied to avoid false positive inflation.

(2017), 'The Modern-Era Retrospective Analysis for Research and Applications, Version 2 (MERRA-2)', Journal of Climate, doi:10.1175/JCLI-D-16-0758.1.
